To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rabbit nictitans CR is elicited by electrical stimulation in all of the four nuclei of the efferent accessory abducens pathway (IO, IP, TRIG, and RN) but that CRs are acquired most readily with EBS in the RN and TRIG.
the rabbit nictitans response can be elicited by electrical stimulation of the brainstem and can be conditioned by electrical stimulation of brain nuclei in the cerebellum and red nucleus.
the rabbit nictitans response to EBS can be elicited in the TRIG nucleus, IP, and the RN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of brainstem nuclei in the conditioning of the nictitating membrane (NM) response.
the acquisition of conditioned responses (CRs) to the nictitating membrane (NM) response in the rabbit.
the role of the cerebellum in the acquisition of conditioned responses and the neural circuitry that mediates these responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebellum is involved in motor learning.
the rabbit nictitans response is a conditioned response and not an unconditioned reflex.
the cerebellum is involved with the acquisition of the rabbit CR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cerebellum is not necessary for CR acquisition, but it does modify the CRs.
the cerebellum and brainstem are both necessary and sufficient for CR acquisition.
the cerebellar circuitry is capable of CR acquisition, and this acquisition can be modified by the CS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RN is an important component for conditioning the NMR.
the cerebellum and its efferent projections to the accessory abducns nucleus can be used to elicit conditioned responses.
the red nucleus is a critical component in the acquisition of the conditioned response.
